one_sentence_story: In 1974, Elizabeth Loftus showed 195 students the exact same car-crash film and proved that changing one word in a question from 'hit' to 'smashed' raised speed estimates by nearly 7 mph and made 32 percent remember broken glass that was never there.
so_what_for_you: Your memory is more like a live Wikipedia page than a locked security recording: every time you pull an old memory up, someone else's wording — or your own retelling — can quietly edit the page and save the changes as fact.
